title: Equal concentrations
hook: Compare the solutions and predict the water flow.

knows: A membrane can allow some substances through but not others.
doesNotKnow: In this isotonic example there is no initial net water movement, although individual water molecules still move in both directions.

misconception: Water always moves toward the side with less solute.
objective: Predict the initial net water direction under the stated osmotic conditions.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: An animal cell starts with 0.2 M nonpenetrating solute inside and 0.2 M outside. The membrane passes water but not this solute. What is the initial net water direction? In this isotonic example there is no initial net water movement, although individual water molecules still move in both directions.
Cell shapes and water arrows are schematic; the concentrations shown are initial values, not values after equilibration.

Recall: With a membrane permeable to water but not solute, which way is initial net water movement when outside has more nonpenetrating solute? Water initially moves toward the side with the higher nonpenetrating-solute concentration under the stated simplified conditions.

recall.question: With a membrane permeable to water but not solute, which way is initial net water movement when outside has more nonpenetrating solute?
recall.why: Water initially moves toward the side with the higher nonpenetrating-solute concentration under the stated simplified conditions.
